author: Isabella Torregiani
title: Trump threatens Nigeria over 'massacred' Christians - NewsBreak
text:
By Isabella Torregiani ,
6 hours ago President Donald Trump is threatening sanctions against Nigeria, claiming its government has failed to protect Christians from violent attacks.
He described the persecution as an “existential threat” to Christianity and has promised to label Nigeria a “country of particular concern” for religious freedom violations.
Persecution claims The alleged persecution of Christians in Nigeria has drawn renewed attention, especially after comedian and political commentator Bill Maher claimed they are being “systematically killed” and criticized Americans for ignoring the crisis.
Nigerian officials have denied the claims, stating that the violence is mainly carried out by extremist groups targeting both Muslims and Christians.
Who’s at risk? Analysts caution that, despite attacks on Christians, Muslims make up most of the casualties in northern Nigeria.
Boko Haram militants and bandits are primarily motivated by control and profit, not faith.
Each spring, the State Department releases its report on international religious freedom, but this year’s numbers have not appeared.
These reports often inform “country of particular concern” decisions, though they aren’t required.
The latest report, under former President Joe Biden for 2023, documented continued violence targeting Christians and Muslims.
Cruz steps in During Trump’s first term in 2020, Nigeria was added to the U.S. religious freedom watchlist for “systematic violations of religious freedom.”
Its removal in 2023 was seen by some as an attempt to smooth relations ahead of a visit by former Secretary of State Antony Blinken.
Ted Cruz recently announced that more than 50,000 Christians have died in Nigeria since 2009.
The Nigerian government has rejected this claim.
On X, the senator stated that Christians have been “massacred” and reported that thousands of churches and schools were destroyed.
Trump’s response On Truth Social, Trump said he intends to list Nigeria as a “country of particular concern” for its record on religious freedom.
“Christianity is facing an existential threat in Nigeria,” Trump said. “Radical Islamists are responsible for this mass slaughter. I am hereby making Nigeria a ‘country of particular concern.’”
He also called on Congress to assess the situation, insisting that the U.S. “cannot stand by while such atrocities are happening” and must act to “save our great Christian population around the world.”
